findings.title: Generic meta-rule namespace can admit a confirmed Domain rule without Domain human authority
findings.failure_condition: A Rule is filed in the generic .codex/meta-rules namespace with category=domain, status=confirmed, owner and approved_at populated, and only a report-type source. The generic Rule schema accepts it; the loader labels it registry=meta; applicable-rule selection rejects only registry=domain or non-confirmed entries, so the Rule becomes applicable without a Domain human approval binding.

reproduction.method: Construct the described Rule in memory and pass it through the production Rule schema and applicable-rule selector without modifying candidate files.

findings.impact: A report, implementation, test, migration, or health artifact can be represented as a confirmed Domain authority through the generic namespace, enabling an incorrect authoritative business decision despite the dedicated Domain registry remaining proposed-only.
findings.required_resolution: Make Domain category authority namespace-independent. Reject every category=domain Rule from generic meta authority, or require a validator-owned Domain approval binding and authoritative source contract before any Domain Rule can be applicable. Add cross-namespace mutation and production-path tests.

a4_closure_entries.reason: Dedicated confirmed-Domain approval was removed, but category=domain authority remains reachable through the generic meta-rule namespace without Domain approval provenance.

Phase 1 no longer claims confirmed Domain approval lookup or promotion. The dedicated approval schema/resolver is absent, so its former uniqueness contract is outside the narrowed candidate; this does not cure the separate generic meta-rule bypass.

candidate_review_gate_recommendation.reason: The generic meta-rule path can grant Domain authority without an approved Domain source and human approval binding.

review_boundary: This review assesses only the Domain Rule governance mechanism. It does not approve any actual railway maintenance rule.
